The Tourne Select Is a High-End Camper Van for Anyone Who Wants Comfort Without the Show
16 photos
Photo: Tourne Campervans
What we have here is a conversion based on a brand-new Fiat Ducato model. Tourne Campervans, based in Pivka, Slovenia, is the company behind this project. It specializes in custom-fitted, all-season-ready camper vans.
After I wrote about Tourne's newest camper van addition, the Expre, I was curious to see what other builds the company offers.
The Select is available in two versions, a 6-meter one and a 6.4-meter one – the only difference is the way you sleep. The shorter version has a crosswise sleeping arrangement, while the longer one has a lengthwise arrangement.
According to its maker, the Tourne Select is fitted out for maximum comfort, performance, and flexibility. Let's see if that's the case, starting, as always, with the exterior.
Tourne shared that it doesn't want the Select to stand out or scream "camper van," but still pack quality features. I'd say it managed to do that, with the rig not screaming camper van as in it will not grab too much attention.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Tourne Campervans That said, it's quite obvious, at least to someone who's seen a camper van before, that the Select is a tiny home on wheels, even though it doesn't have that many upgrades.
The van rides on black alloy wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. On top, you'll come across solar panels and a large awning. Other notable mods are power and water hook-ups and a compartment that lets you access the toilet from the outside.
Enter, and a bright interior will greet you. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases that allow you to turn them around to face the back of the van.
Regarding aesthetics, you'll notice laminated cabinetry with a light grain finish, black flooring, and white walls with a matching ceiling. Most of the furniture is created in-house from wood and hand-assembled in the company's shop.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Tourne Campervans Straight ahead as you enter, you'll discover a seating area. It comprises a dual bench seat and a table, with a large overhead cabinet above. The seating area has Tourne's patented bed system called the Dream4.
Long story short, you can use slide-outs and several panels that come together like puzzle pieces to transform the seating area into a bed that can sleep two kids or even two adults if they don't mind a snug fit.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side, by the entrance. It features a deep black stainless steel sink with a cover, a portable single-burner induction stove, and a tall 78-liter Thetford fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
A spice rack, a lower cabinet with adjustable shelves, several drawers, and a sizeable overhead cabinet are available for storage. One of the drawers doubles as a slide-out countertop, as it has a removable top.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Tourne Campervans Of course, a deluxe camper van like the Select will offer one of the most sought-after amenities in a home on wheels: a bathroom, hidden behind a white retractable door. It boasts a toilet, a skylight that can be opened, and a small corner sink with a pull-out faucet that can double as a showerhead.
A distinctive touch in the bathroom is that the toilet is mounted on a swivel base so you can turn it around to use it and turn it back to create more space when unused. Moreover, the bathroom can double as a drying area, as it has a vent pumping hot air.
The rear part of the interior is taken up by a large bedroom. Even though it's not fully divided from the rest of the living space, the bedroom does feel like a separate room because of the kitchen and bathroom wall panels that partly close it off. The bedroom also offers two large overhead cabinets, two shelves, and charging points.
Tourne Campervans came up with a clever setup to be able to utilize the space in the back. The bed platform is made up of three panels that can be raised and strapped to the cabinets on the driver's side.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Tourne Campervans Two boxes on the sides hold the bed platform panels, offer extra storage space, and accommodate the utility systems.
Power is on the left side – unfortunately, we don't know the exact battery capacity, but we do know that it's enough to sustain off-grid travel.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a heated 90-liter (23-gallon) freshwater tank above the passenger-side wheel well and a heated and insulated 100-liter (26-gallon) greywater tank underneath the van.
Traveling in colder environments is not an issue in this rig, as it sports not one but two heaters. The first is a Truma Combi heater that offers both hot water and heated air, while also powering a heated floor system. The second is a Webasto diesel-powered air heater.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Tourne Campervans The control panel for the rig's utilities is conveniently located above the entrance. It includes a touchscreen display that lets you monitor and control the power system and a digital thermostat for the Truma heater.
All in all, the Tourne Select creates ideal home-like conditions for you on the road, letting you go off-grid in comfort and style. There's one more thing to mention, one that makes the camper van an even more attractive offering: the price.
The starting price of the Select is £84,507 ($112,774) for the 6-meter version or £86,607 ($115,577) for the 6.4-meter one. To be fair, these are the prices I managed to find from last year – it's best to check in with the company for updated information.
